author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
sources.targetFrame: Independent micro scene; source coordinates unchanged

derivative.method: Byte-for-byte original; on-demand rendering of every original parent edge. No synthesized surface, radius or synapse.

sources.attribution: Allen Cell Types; NeuroMorpho.Org (RRID:SCR_002145), neuron 102401; Koch and Jones (2016); Tecuatl, Ljungquist and Ascoli (2024).
sources.identity: API identifies human Male adult 30, principal Spiny cell, moderate dendrite/axon integrity. Do not infer an exact cortical gyrus from conflicting regional metadata. Original Vaa3D header contains processing directory 639385197; this is retained, not silently relabelled as a second specimen. Both original and repository CNG files have identical non-soma point counts per type (8092 axon, 3477 basal, 6420 apical); CNG adds two soma points and changes coordinates, so it is not the geometry reference.
limitations: Soma point is a marker, not a radius-faithful cell surface

author: Heidi Schlehlein
sources.sourceFrame: Original glTF model coordinates; schematic scale, not a donor histological measurement
sources.targetFrame: Independent micro scene; all original transforms unchanged

derivative.method: Lossless Meshopt only. No vertex reordering, quantization, decimation, repair or coordinate transform. All decoded attributes compared byte-for-byte; each ordered triangle retains its three indices and winding (Meshopt may cyclically rotate a triangle). Graph, transforms, material properties and bounds preserved.

sources.attribution: Heidi Schlehlein; Katy Börner (project lead); Sanjay Jain (reviewer), Human Reference Atlas 2026, CC BY 4.0. Lossless geometry compression for MED3D.
sources.identity: Human educational schematic based on bibliography and expert review, not female or male donor segmentation. 18 identified source meshes: two arterioles, capillary network and 15 podocytes. NIH displayed polygon count refers to a last subobject; actual source total is 1,646,925 triangles.
limitations: Not registered into either body kidney
